co_honeycomb_spire.blurb: A small formation on the rim of Castlewood Canyon State Park, in the Denver South part of the state, named for the little tower that carries a single bolt on its summit. Its twelve climbs are mostly top-rope setups plus a handful of trad lines, running from easy fifth class into the low 5.12 range, with the biggest cluster at 5.10. The gentlest cracks make it a sensible place to learn trad placements, while the harder top-ropes give stronger climbers something to work on. It sits a short stroll from the southern entrance lot, yet few climbers seem to bother, so it tends to be a quiet corner of the park.

co_humphrey_s_dome.blurb: A granite dome in the Buffalo Creek area of the South Platte, rising above a hillside of burned trees and scattered boulders. All twelve routes are trad, spanning 5.7 up to a single 5.11, with five at 5.10; most follow cracks and slabs, and the best-known line is a long crack on the south face. The dome sees little traffic and the setting feels quiet, so it suits a climber who wants solitude rather than a crowded cliff. Expect a full day built around a lengthy hike, and bring your own judgment about the older fixed gear.

co_magic_kingdom.blurb: A small, broken cluster of rocks in the Bigfoots area off Rampart Range Road, just south of The Stacks. Most of its twelve climbs are short top-ropes, with a few trad leads, a pair of bolted lines and one boulder problem. Grades run from easy scrambling up to 5.11, with a good share at 5.9 and below. Faces mostly look southeast to east, and rigging a top-rope often means slinging a boulder on the summit. This is a place for easy mileage, practice and scrambling rather than a destination for hard climbing.

co_hole_in_the_wall.blurb: A north-facing wall in the West Valley section of Devil's Head, in the South Platte, set in a gully beside Crag Ranch. The twelve routes split evenly between sport and trad, running from 5.8 into the 5.12 range, with most between 5.10 and 5.11. Shade lasts nearly all day, which makes it a handy escape when the sunnier walls are baking. The stone is dark and in places mossy, and the cracks and holds on the busier lines are clean. Come ready for steady, sustained climbing in the middle grades.

co_piranha_boulder.blurb: A compact bouldering spot in the Jaws area of the Weller section on the Aspen side of Independence Pass, sitting directly across from the Jaws Boulder. Twelve problems run from V0 to V5; four are V0, a few sit around V2, and the top end is a short group of V4 and V5 lines. The rock includes a lower boulder with right-leaning edges and seams, a detached block, and a steeper overhanging section to the right. It is a small stop that combines well with other boulders nearby, best for a short session rather than a full day.

co_gollum_s_cave.blurb: A secluded alcove in the Grottos area of Independence Pass, a short walk from the day-use lot east of Aspen. The lines are short and steep, and the cave mixes five sport routes at 5.10 to 5.12, three trad lines and four boulder problems, from a couple of V2s to a few much harder ones around V9 and above. The cave has two sections: the lower one is met first coming from the west, and the upper one catches more sun. Bugs can be bad in summer, and a small boggy pond sits beside the roof.
co_gollum_s_cave.parking_note: Leave the car in the Grottos day-use lot beside the highway east of Aspen; the cave is reached on foot from there.

co_goal_post_boulder.blurb: A big boulder in the Grottos area of Independence Pass, east of Aspen, with a dozen mostly semi-high problems on excellent rock. Grades run from V0 to V4: four V0s and two V1s make up the easy end, then a V2, a V3 and four V4s. The landings are flat and safe, so it works well for newer boulderers and for moderate climbers looking for a friendly session. It sits near the neighbouring Lesoterica Boulder, which makes it simple to string together a morning of problems in one spot.
